Color

Theme tokens for new work, plus the legacy Material palette.

RoutePlate ships two color systems. New styles should use the Material Design 3 tokens — CSS custom properties on :root named --md-sys-color-*, exposed as utility classes like .primary and .on-surface-text. The older .red.lighten-2 palette is still generated for compatibility.

Token values follow the page theme. The docs site sets <html theme="light"> or theme="dark". Without that attribute, the tokens follow prefers-color-scheme.

A background class sets background-color. Append -text for color. Pair a fill with its on-* text class so contrast stays correct when the theme flips.

.primary
.on-primary
.primary-container
.on-primary-container
.secondary
.tertiary
.error
.surface-variant
<div class="primary on-primary-text">.primary</div>
<span class="on-surface-text">.on-surface-text</span>

The named utilities are:

primary, on-primary, primary-container, on-primary-container, secondary, on-secondary, secondary-container, on-secondary-container, tertiary, on-tertiary, tertiary-container, on-tertiary-container, error, on-error, error-container, on-error-container, background, on-background, surface, on-surface, surface-variant, on-surface-variant, outline, outline-variant, inverse-surface, inverse-on-surface, inverse-primary, shadow, surface-tint, scrim.

Each name is a background class. The same name plus -text is the foreground class (.primary-text, .on-surface-text).

In Sass, consume the token directly. Do not write rgba(var(--md-sys-color-primary), 0.06) — the tokens hold hex colors, so that form is invalid. Mix with transparency instead: 

.my-tint {
  background-color: var(--md-sys-color-primary);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-primary);
}

.my-overlay {
  background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--md-sys-color-primary) 6%, transparent);
}

Usage

The legacy palette is the Material Design 2014 ramps: a color name plus an optional lighten-*, darken-*, or accent-* class. Prefer the token utilities above for new work.

Background Color

Add the color name and, if you need a shade, the lighten/darken/accent class.

This is a card panel with a teal lighten-2 class
<div class="card-panel teal lighten-2">This is a card panel with a teal lighten-2 class</div>
Text Color

Append -text to the color name. Shade modifiers on text use a text- prefix: text-darken-2, text-lighten-1, text-accent-2.

This is a card panel with dark blue text 
<div class="card-panel">
  <span class="blue-text text-darken-2">This is a card panel with dark blue text</span>
</div>

black, white, and transparent are standalone classes (and -text variants). There is also routeplate-red with lighten/darken shades (no accents) — that is the rebranded Materialize red ramp.

Sass

Do not @extend these classes across files — that is how the old stylesheet lost control of cascade order. In a component partial, call colorFunc("blue", "lighten-4") or set the MD3 token. 

.ilike-blue-container {
  background-color: colorFunc("blue", "lighten-4");
  color: colorFunc("blue", "darken-2");
}

colorFunc($color, $type) reads the $colors map. $type is "base", "lighten-5" … "lighten-1", "darken-1" … "darken-4", or "accent-1" … "accent-4" when that ramp has accents.
